title: "The R package giniVarCI"
subtitle: "Gini indices, variances and confidence intervals for finite and infinite populations"

**giniVarCI** is the open-source R package developed in GiniUs (objective OG3). It is available on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=giniVarCI) and on [R-universe](https://jfmunozrosas.r-universe.dev/giniVarCI), where it can also be used in the browser with webR (see the [R exercises](practice.qmd)).

> Muñoz, J.F., Pavía, J.M., & Álvarez-Verdejo, E. (2024). *giniVarCI: Gini Indices, Variances and Confidence Intervals for Finite and Infinite Populations*. R package version 0.0.1-3. <https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.giniVarCI>

## What it does

1. Estimates the Gini index for samples from **infinite populations** (`igini()`, `iginindex()`) and from **finite populations** with survey weights or inclusion probabilities (`fgini()`, `fginindex()`), with the different expressions of the literature.
2. Computes **variances and confidence intervals** with different methods: percentile and BCa bootstrap, jackknife, linearisation and empirical likelihood (`igini()`, `fgini()`), and compares them (`icompareCI()`, `fcompareCI()`).
3. Computes the **Gini index of continuous probability distributions** (Beta, Burr, chi-squared, Dagum, F, Fisk, Gamma, Gompertz, lognormal, Pareto, etc.: functions `gbeta()`, `gdagum()`, `ggamma()`, ...).
4. Draws **samples with a Gini index set by the user** (`gsample()`), very useful for simulation studies.
5. Uses **Rcpp** (C++), so calculations are faster than in other packages that compute the Gini index.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("giniVarCI")            # from CRAN
library(giniVarCI)
vignette("GiniVarInterval", package = "giniVarCI")
```

## Examples

**Infinite populations.**

```r
set.seed(123)
y <- gsample(n = 100, gini = 0.5, distribution = "lognormal")

igini(y)                             # Gini index (with bias correction)
iginindex(y, method = 5)             # a specific expression of the Gini index
igini(y, interval = "zjackknife")    # jackknife interval
igini(y, interval = "BCa")           # BCa bootstrap interval
igini(y, interval = "ELchisq")       # empirical likelihood interval
icompareCI(y, plotCI = TRUE)         # compares all the intervals
```

Intervals available in `igini()`: `"pbootstrap"`, `"BCa"`, `"zjackknife"`, `"tjackknife"`, `"zalinearization"`, `"zblinearization"`, `"talinearization"`, `"tblinearization"`, `"ELchisq"` and `"ELboot"`.

**Finite populations (survey data).**

```r
data(eusilc, package = "laeken")
y <- eusilc$eqIncome[eusilc$db040 == "Burgenland"]
w <- eusilc$rb050[eusilc$db040 == "Burgenland"]

fgini(y, w)                                    # weighted Gini index
fginindex(y, w, method = 3)                    # Berger (2008), mid-point distribution function
fgini(y, w, interval = "zjackknife")           # jackknife interval
fgini(y, w, interval = "zalinearization")      # linearisation interval
```

Methods available in `fginindex()`: 1, Langel and Tillé (2013); 2 (default), Alfons and Templ (2012) and Langel and Tillé (2013); 3, Berger (2008); 4, Berger and Gedik-Balay (2020); 5, Lerman and Yitzhaki (1989).
